limitations: 25 individuals/20 families, 16 recessive variants. Association supported by multiple segregating homozygous families and animal perturbations, but functional experiments test only selected alleles/cell lines; no clinical rescue or isogenic correction. Onset/assessment ages and identifiers internally inconsistent: P2 onset15/assessment29 in main versus7/21 vignette; P13 death3main versus3.5supplement; P17 Table14y versus onset13+2y followup. Figure2 caption F15II3 differs pedigree/vignette II2.

Main methods NM032900.6/NP116289.4 versus Figure1/S2 NM001136035/NP001129507. Same c./p. names support association but transcript equivalence not independently remapped. P2 His196Thrfs10 in S2/packet versus His196Glnfs9 in main; genomic repeat normalization unresolved. P20 source chr10:97263470 and VCF97263469CG>C versus packet HGVS97263471del unresolved normalization. F9 c452del/main versus c479del/S2 and Asn160Metfs21 versus *2 inconsistent. Do not silently normalize.

All variants called P/LP in main but S2 Met1? and Pro273Leu classified VUS. Main AlphaMissense7/9 differs S4 8/9 (only Asn29Asp benign). Main 3/23=9% is arithmetic error (13%). Positive calculated free-energy change is destabilizing by supplementary methods/Figure3; narrative describes direction backwards for six variants and Q151K. Predictors not clinical proof.

Purified isolated GAP domains G140D/Q151K/H196fs abolish measured activity; equal1.5microgram mass rather than equal molarity for truncated domain. Dominant loss-of-function wording does not establish dominant inheritance or dominant-negative mechanism; pedigrees recessive, no WT-mutant competition test. Asn29Asp migration assay is not direct GAP assay.

Patient fibroblast RNA/protein abundance not significantly altered; iPSC motor-neuron protein reduced in G140D/L68P lines with two controls. No direct RhoA/ROCK activation measurement, no isogenic rescue. Fibroblast migration reduced N29D/G140D but not L68P; MTT no increase. Motor-neuron branch counts use5–10 cells/genotype nested within few lines; cells not independent patients.

Fly whole-body RNAi/degradation/knockout locomotor phenotypes, but tissue-specific neuronal/glial/muscle/neuroblast knockdown does not recapitulate overall locomotor deficit. Knockout compared heterozygous controls; no human-allele rescue. Fish F0 mosaic crispants are not stable homozygous mutants; full dose body-length reduction can confound swimming distance/velocity, which are dependent outcomes. Birefringence n3 nonsignificant is not proof of normal muscle. Selected off-target Sanger and unchanged transcript levels cannot exclude all off-target effects.

P7 sensory loss explicitly in vignette but sensory involvement No in mainTable1; preserve internal conflict. P17 CIDP/IVIG response unclear, acute trauma context; P6 immunoglobulin ongoing, not established effective. All mapped cases match recessive neuropathy but labels CMT2/mixed/demyelinating/motor subtypes vary and are not interchangeable.

Blot supplementary caption patient order C1 C2 P5 P11 P6 C3 differs mainFigure4B labels C1 C2 P5 P6 P11 C3; source of lane-label discrepancy unresolved without unedited pixel inspection. Supplementary figures, image-only final table, unedited blot pixels and three omics/plot-source spreadsheets unread; no complete-component claim.
